## Iron Infusion Referrals

To receive an iron infusion at The Iron Infusion Clinic, patients are required to have a referral
from a General Practitioner (GP) or a Specialist. If you have been diagnosed with iron deficiency
and are considering an iron infusion, please consult with your doctor. Your healthcare provider can
assess your condition and, if an infusion is deemed appropriate, they will provide you with the
necessary referral. Once you have your referral, you can contact us to schedule your appointment. We
are here to support you through your treatment journey and help you restore your iron levels to a
healthy balance.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Is iron infusion therapy right for me?

Determining whether iron infusion therapy is the appropriate treatment for your needs involves a
comprehensive evaluation of several factors. These factors include your medical history, current
health status, and importantly, the recommendations of your healthcare provider.

Before making a decision, your healthcare provider will conduct blood tests to assess your iron
levels and overall blood health. This step is crucial to ensure that iron deficiency is indeed the
cause of your symptoms and to determine the severity of the deficiency.

It’s essential to have an open discussion with your healthcare provider about your symptoms,
concerns, and treatment preferences. This conversation is vital to ascertain if iron infusion
therapy suits your specific health scenario. Your provider will consider various factors such as the
effectiveness of previous treatments like oral iron supplements, your body’s ability to tolerate
these supplements, and any underlying health conditions that might affect treatment options.

Your healthcare provider will also consider your symptoms’ severity, how quickly you need to
increase your iron levels, and any previous adverse reactions to iron supplements. All these
elements help in determining if iron infusion therapy is not just a viable option, but the right one
for you, tailored to offer the most benefit with the least risk.

What exactly happens during an iron infusion?

During your infusion appointment, your nurse will discuss the iron infusion treatment, ask some
questions, go through the consent form with you and answer any questions you may have.

Prior to starting the infusion, your nurse will measure and record your heart rate, blood pressure
and temperature. A cannula (small plastic tube) will then be inserted (via a needle) into a vein in
your arm, and connected to a sterile bag containing the iron. Your nurse will will continue to
monitor you, however we ask that you inform the nurse should you feel unwell or experience any side
effects during the infusion.

You will also be monitored for any delayed reactions for 30 minutes after the infusion has finished.
We ask that you inform the nurse if you feel unwell during this time. Following the 30 minute
observation period, the cannula will be removed and you can go home.

Is the process painful?

An iron infusion is generally not considered painful, however some people may experience mild
discomfort at the injection site. Some individuals may experience minor bruising or tenderness where
the needle was inserted.

Are there different types of iron infusions?

In Australia there are several types of iron infusion formulations available. Each type has its
specific indications, dosage requirements, and administration protocols, which are determined based
on the patient’s individual health needs and medical history. It is important to discuss with your
healthcare provider which iron infusion is most appropriate for their condition.

The Iron Infusion Clinic accepts referrals for the two most commonly prescribed iron formulations.
The other types are typically administered in an inpatient (in hospital) setting.

Do I need more than one iron infusion?

The number of iron infusions needed will vary from person to person and will depend on the severity
of the iron deficiency. Your GP or Specialist will determine your dosage based on your blood test
results and weight. For most patients, a single infusion or a series of two infusions spread over 2
weeks will be enough to correct the deficiency. 

In some cases, the cause of the deficiency may persist, meaning a person may require regular
infusions to maintain health iron levels. It is important for patients to closely follow their
healthcare provider’s recommendations and attend all follow-up appointments with their GP or
Specialist to assess how well their iron levels are being restored.



How long will my iron infusion take?

The iron infusion will take 15 to 30 minutes, however please allow 60 minutes in total for your
appointment as there is a 30 minute observation period post infusion.

Do I need to do anything to prepare for my iron infusion?

**Hydration:** It is important to be well hydrated prior to your iron infusion, we recommend to
drink 2 to 3 glasses of water prior to your appointment. Staying well hydrated will help your nurse
locate a suitable vein. 

**Clothing:** It is recommended to wear comfortable, layered, loose-fitting clothing. If you are
wearing long sleeves, they will  need to be loose enough to be pushed up above your elbow. 

You are not required to fast before your infusion, and you can take your normal medications prior to
an iron infusion. Iron tablets / liquid however should be stopped 7 days before. 

What do I need to disclose prior to my iron infusion?

Ensure that you advise your nurse if you:
* Are pregnant
* Are taking any medications or herbal supplements
* Have any liver conditions
* Have experienced excess iron levels in the past
* Are feeling unwell or have an infection
* Have been taking oral iron supplements
* Have had an anaphylactic reaction to an iron infusion in the past
* If you have heart or kidney failure
* Have had multiple iron infusions in the past 12 months

Should I stop taking my oral iron supplements before and after my infusion?

Please cease oral iron supplements (tablets or liquid) a week before your iron infusion. 

Your referring GP or Specialist will likely wish to see you again for follow up blood tests 2 to 4
weeks after your iron infusion, therefore please contact your GP or Specialist to determine whether
an appointment is required. 

Can I drive myself to my iron infusion appointment?

Yes. We require all patients who receive an iron infusion to wait within the clinic for 30 minutes
following their infusion so that we can monitor any potential side effects. Following this period,
you will be able to drive home.

What do I need to bring to my iron infusion?

We recommend to bring:
* An electronic device, book or magazine to keep you entertained during the treatment (WiFi
  available). Please bring headphones if you wish to listen to music or watch a movie etc.
* A cardigan or blanket to provide warmth if required

Do I need to fast before my iron infusion?

No, you do not need to fast before your iron infusion. Eat all your regular meals and continue
taking your regular medication.

Please ensure you are well hydrated prior to your iron infusion.

What is iron staining?

Iron staining is a potential risk of an iron infusion. It occurs when the iron solution leaks from
the vein into the surrounding tissue during the infusion process, which can result in a brownish
stain to the skin around the injection site and arm. While iron staining is uncommon, it can be
**long-lasting or permanent**. 

Before the infusion, we educate our patients on what to expect and encourage them to inform us
immediately if they feel any discomfort or burning sensation at the infusion site, which can be an
early sign of infiltration.

At The Iron Infusion Clinic, we take several measures to minimise the risk of iron staining. By
taking these precautions, we strive to provide a safe and effective treatment experience.

Are there any side effects of iron infusions?

As with all medicines and medical procedures, there are risks and complications associated with iron
infusions. Risks include, but are not limited to:

The most common side effects include:
* Headaches
* Dizziness
* Flu like symptoms
* Flushes
* Nausea
* Bruising or skin reaction at the infusion site

Uncommon side effects include:
* Skin staining (see above)
* Stomach upsets
* Temporary changes in taste – some people experience a metallic taste
* Changes in your blood pressure
* Changes in your pulse
* Muscle or joint pains, backache and muscle cramps
* Tiredness, chills, chest pain, swelling, pins and needles, high temperature, itching, rash
* Shortness of breath

# Welcome to MEDIX

## Hello!

Welcome to our page! We are MEDIX, a luxury concierge service, and we specialize in premium
on-demand in home medical and aesthetic services in New York City and surrounding areas including
Upstate New York, Long Island/Hamptons area, New Jersey, and Connecticut. Under our 24/7 concierge
model, our patients and clients can access convenient and flexible medical care and aesthetic
services at the comfort of their home, offices, hotel rooms, backstages, and more.

Founded in 2018, MEDIX has proudly provided 24/7 medical and health services such as house call
doctor visits, primary care services, urgent care services, telemedicine, and IV therapy to
thousands of patients in the Tri-State area. In March 2020, MEDIX widened its scope of practice in
response to the COVID-19 pandemic, providing extensive testing and doctor services to patients as
well as institutions such as nursing homes and corporations affected by the crisis, while continuing
routine medical treatments for our primary care and IV Therapy patients.

In 2023, MEDIX is excited to announce the launch of [Lavender Palette][46], our beauty and wellness
division of the company. We model Lavender Palette after our medical counterpart, and strive to
provide personally curated, hassle-free, and around the clock services at the comfort of your home.


# Luxury should be hassle-free.

## House Calls - The Concierge Model

Every service we provide here at MEDIX is offered as a house call! Our team of medical and aesthetic
practitioners will travel to the location of your choice on an on demand basis. Our goal and mission
is to remove the inconveniences traditionally associated with scheduling, long-wait time, and
inflexibility, so we can help you streamline your everyday health and wellness journey.

Not only do our practitioners have years of experiences in their respective field, they are also
highly experienced in providing their services as house calls. Here at MEDIX, we vouch to maintain a
high standard of service regardless of the location and circumstances.

### Become Part OF the MEDIX Family!

Who We Are

## Houston's Premier
## Freestanding Emergency Room

Memorial Heights Emergency Center has served the Houston Heights, River Oaks, Midtown, and Downtown
communities since November 2009. We combine the full support services of a hospital ER with the
aesthetics and convenience of a high-end private practice.

Our 6,000+ sq ft facility includes eight treatment rooms — several equipped with crash carts and
defibrillators — and a CLIA-certified in-house lab with CT scan, Ultrasound, and X-ray for immediate
on-site diagnostics.
* Board-certified, residency-trained emergency physicians only
* No appointment needed — walk in 24 hours a day, 7 days a week
* Priority transfer privileges with all local Houston hospitals
* 300+ medications stocked in our in-house pharmacy
* We work with your private insurance to minimize out-of-pocket costs

### Hear from Dr Huzefa Bahrain, a Hematologist-Oncologist

Dr Bahrain explains why he uses Monoferric to treat IDA.


See transcript

**I’m Dr. Huzefa Bahrain, welcome to Monoferric Moments.**

I practice hematology and oncology in Baltimore. We operate an erythropoiesis center where we treat
a wide variety of patients with various iron deficiency anemia etiologies. They can range from
bariatric surgery patients to heart failure, to pregnancy.

Monoferric is an intravenous iron replacement therapy that can be given in just 1 single dose,
delivering 1000 milligrams.

In my experience, we find that for most patients, just 1 dose of 1000 milligrams of Monoferric is
sufficient to replace iron stores. If iron deficiency anemia reoccurs, a repeat dose would be
necessary.

I use Monoferric in my practice because of its overall combination of 1-dose administration,
efficacy, tolerability, and patient support services.

For more information, explore [Monoferric.com][88]

### Have questions about Monoferric?

Sign up to contact a representative.

[Contact us][89]

### Innovative matrix controls bioavailable iron release

Monoferric is **FDA approved for one infusion in as little as 20 minutes** that delivers a slow and
controlled release of bioavailable iron for patients with IDA.^{1,2,a}

^{a}Repeat dose if IDA reoccurs.

[Learn about controlled iron release][90]

### Pharmacosmos has over 60 years’ experience researching and developing innovative treatments

Monoferric was introduced more than 10 years ago as Monofer® in the EU. Monofer is available in more
than 55 countries and more than 68 million doses have been administered (as defined by the WHO
definition of 100-mg doses).

### 1 dose of Monoferric vs up to 5 doses of iron sucrose

The safety and efficacy of Monoferric for treatment of IDA were evaluated in two randomized,
open-label, noninferiority, actively controlled clinical trials performed in a total of 3050
patients with IDA of different etiologies.^{3,4}

[See the results][91]

### 1000 mg IV iron in a single infusion in ≥20 minutes^{b}

Monoferric offers iron infusion in one dose in a single 1000-mg vial for patients weighing 50 kg or
more.¹ Monoferric is FDA approved to administer 1000 mg in ≥20 minutes.

^{b}Repeat dose if IDA reoccurs.

INDICATIONS

Monoferric is indicated for the treatment of iron deficiency anemia (IDA) in adult patients:
* who have intolerance to oral iron or have had unsatisfactory response to oral iron
* who have non-hemodialysis dependent chronic kidney disease (NDD-CKD)

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION

CONTRAINDICATIONS

Monoferric is contraindicated in patients with a history of serious hypersensitivity to Monoferric
or any of its components. Reactions have included shock, clinically significant hypotension, loss of
consciousness, and/or collapse.

WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS

Hypersensitivity Reactions

Serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylactic-type reactions, some of which have been
life-threatening and fatal, have been reported in patients receiving Monoferric. Patients may
present with shock, clinically significant hypotension, loss of consciousness, and/or collapse.
Monitor patients for signs and symptoms of hypersensitivity during and after Monoferric
administration for at least 30 minutes and until clinically stable following completion of the
infusion. Only administer Monoferric when personnel and therapies are immediately available for the
treatment of serious hypersensitivity reactions. Monoferric is contraindicated in patients with
prior serious hypersensitivity reactions to Monoferric or any of its components. In clinical trials
in patients with IDA and CKD, serious or severe hypersensitivity were reported in 0.3% (6/2008) of
the Monoferric treated subjects. These included 3 events of hypersensitivity in 3 patients; 2 events
of infusion-related reactions in 2 patients and 1 event of asthma in one patient.

Iron Overload

**I’m Dr. Huzefa Bahrain, welcome to Monoferric Moments.**

I practice hematology and oncology in Baltimore. We operate an erythropoiesis center where we treat
a wide variety of patients with various iron deficiency anemia etiologies. They can range from
bariatric surgery patients to heart failure, to pregnancy.

Monoferric is an intravenous iron replacement therapy that can be given in just 1 single dose,
delivering 1000 milligrams.

sufficient to replace iron stores. If iron deficiency anemia reoccurs, a repeat dose would be
necessary.

efficacy, tolerability, and patient support services.

We successfully completed the 11th International Summit on Food, Nutrition and Health in Scotland in
December 2025 under the theme Target 2030: Food and Nutrition Policy - From Human to Planetary
Health.


Please take some time to check the [photos][116] from the event, the outstanding [abstracts][117] we
received, and how our [programme][118] went.


Please also take a moment to learn about our [2026 Summit here][119].

## Establishment of a Scottish hub

NNEdPro has an established and growing presence in Scotland, building on longstanding roots in
clinical and public health nutrition and strengthened by the opening of our strategy office in
Dundee.

 

Since then, we have developed a strong regional network, delivered impactful community programmes
through the Mobile Teaching Kitchen, and formed strategic partnerships with leading academic,
community, and policy organisations.

 

From large-scale events such as the 11th International Summit on Food, Nutrition and Health to local
culinary education initiatives reaching over a thousand community members, our work in Scotland
reflects a commitment to collaboration, innovation, and sustainable impact, with plans to further
expand our reach and contribution in the years ahead.


Learn more about our Scottish hub [here][120].

## Establishment of a Scottish hub

NNEdPro has an established and growing presence in Scotland, building on longstanding roots in
clinical and public health nutrition and strengthened by the opening of our strategy office in
Dundee.

 

Since then, we have developed a strong regional network, delivered impactful community programmes
through the Mobile Teaching Kitchen, and formed strategic partnerships with leading academic,
community, and policy organisations.

 

From large-scale events such as the 11th International Summit on Food, Nutrition and Health to local
culinary education initiatives reaching over a thousand community members, our work in Scotland
reflects a commitment to collaboration, innovation, and sustainable impact, with plans to further
expand our reach and contribution in the years ahead.

[ [Welcome to the show! In this first episode of a 2 part series, we sit down with Claire Chang, a
professional who executed one a compelling career pivot: moving from a dedicated Biomedical
Scientist to an expert in Business Continuity and Risk Management within a law firm. Claire shares
her extraordinary professional journey, detailing how the analytical rigour and attention to detail
required in the lab were some of the transferable skills she needed to succeed in the new role. We
discuss the challenge of mastering new compliance frameworks, how she learned to communicate complex
risk scenarios to different stakeholders, and the unique challenges of maintaining operational
resilience in a regulated environment. Follow for more in part 2!]
From lab coat to law firm: Biomedical Scientist to business continuity with Claire Chang [Part 1]
][110]
[ [In this second session of the Only Cells Antibody Identification (ABID) webinar series, the focus
was on some weird and wonderful cases and techniques. Everything from Chido/Rogers, Knopps to D and
C being G. This session is ideal for biomedical scientists, transfusion practitioners, and trainees
looking to consolidate their understanding of red cell antibody identification in a case-based,
practical format. Session 1, Tools of the trade can be seen here: https://youtu.be/7oMnxJO9B68
Session 2, Putting it into practice can be seen here: https://youtu.be/NDTBxN9YsNA Presented by:
Helen Thom – Biomedical Scientist and RCI Development Lead, NHSBT Hosted by: Anas Nasir – Founder,
OnlyCells]
Antibody identification [3/3] - The weird and the wonderful
][111]
[ [The full video of the second webinar in the Antibody Identification series can be found here:
https://youtu.be/NDTBxN9YsNA This video is a recording of case 4, which we were unable to cover live
during the session.]
Antibody Identification [2/3] - Putting it into practice - Case 4
][112]
[ [In this second session of the Only Cells Antibody Identification (ABID) webinar series, we begin
with a quick recap of the key techniques covered in Session 1: Tools of the Trade. We then apply
those principles in practice by working through three real-life antibody identification cases. Each
case is designed to build confidence in interpreting panels, applying inclusion/exclusion logic, and
approaching complex serological investigations. This session is ideal for biomedical scientists,
transfusion practitioners, and trainees looking to consolidate their understanding of red cell
antibody identification in a case-based, practical format. Case 4 can be seen here:
https://youtu.be/q-alAccGns8 Presented by: Helen Thom – Biomedical Scientist and RCI Development
Lead, NHSBT Hosted by: Anas Nasir – Founder, OnlyCells]
Antibody Identification [2/3] - Putting it into practice
][113]
[ [Welcome to Part 1 of our Antibody Identification (ABID) webinar series, hosted by Only Cells. In
this session, Helen Thom (RCI Development Lead, NHSBT) takes us through the fundamental tools and
techniques used in antibody investigations, including: - Panel cells - The Indirect Antiglobulin
Test (IAT) - Enzyme techniques - Grading reactions - Inclusion and exclusion logic - DAT and elution
methods - Phenotyping vs genotyping This webinar is ideal for trainees, newly qualified biomedical
scientists, and anyone looking to refresh their knowledge of transfusion science. CPD certificates
were issued to all live attendees. Future sessions in this series will build on the content covered
here. To stay updated on future webinars, register for the OnlyCells mailing list at
https://onlycells.co.uk Speaker: Helen Thom – Biomedical Scientist and RCI Development Lead, NHS
Blood and Transplant (NHSBT) Host: Anas Nasir – Founder of OnlyCells, Specialist Biomedical
Scientist]
Antibody Identification [1/3] – Tools of the Trade
][114]
[ [A junior doctor, a major bleed, and a very calm biomedical scientist, what could possibly go
wrong? In this episode of Life in the Lab, we follow a real-time transfusion request from cardiac
theatre. With lives on the line, it’s clear communication, not panic, that keeps things moving. Sam
handles the pressure like a pro, asking all the right questions to ensure safe, effective blood
provision. Because in transfusion, mistakes aren’t just paperwork — they’re patient safety. Whether
you're on the phone or on the bench, clarity saves lives. 👩‍🔬 Created by a real biomedical scientist
🎓 Based on everyday lab reality with a dose of humour 🩸 Subscribe for new episodes showing life
behind the blood films]

# We are Pharmacosmos

We want to change the way iron deficiency is prevented and treated.

Watch the film
[Explore Pharmacosmos][25]
Pharmacosmos is...

A global pioneer in carbohydrate chemistry and a leader in the development of innovative treatments
for patients suffering from iron deficiency and iron deficiency anaemia.

## Who we are

As a family-held company, we are cognisant of how work shapes who we are and who we aspire to
become.

## Our focus

We develop innovative treatments for unmet patient needs, with a focus on iron metabolism and
blood-related disorders.

## Programmes

We are developing petadeferitrin, a new iron chelator for iron overload due to frequent blood
transfusions and other iron-related conditions, drawing on our expertise in iron metabolism.

## Life at Pharmacosmos

We prioritise ensuring an inclusive and appreciative culture that helps us connect better as a team.
This makes it easier for us to tackle tough conversations and make brave decisions together.

## Career

We are a fully integrated pharmaceutical company with many exciting opportunities ahead of us. Do
you want to join us?

## News & Media

Stay informed about what is happening at Pharmacosmos.

## Global presence

Our global presence is strong, thanks to our skilled colleagues and partners in all the major
pharmaceutical markets. Today, we are represented in more than 40 countries.

# Multispecialty care — built by doctors, not corporations.

Board-certified specialty and primary care across Greater Houston & Texas — physician-owned, same
clinician every visit, one shared record.

[Book a visit][48][Find a location][49]

## What is Remix Medical?

Most healthcare runs on a corporate clock. The pieces — your primary doctor, your specialists, your
pharmacy, your hospital — all exist, but they don’t talk to each other, and the people making
decisions about your care aren’t the ones sitting across from you.

> Eight-minute visits, rotating providers, corporate referral loops — Remix Medical threw them out,
> then rebuilt around technology that connects, communication that works, and clinicians who stay.

We’re a **physician-owned, independent multispecialty practice based in [Houston, Texas][51]** —
meaning your doctor decides your treatment, you see the same clinician every visit, and complex
cases get coordinated across specialists in [nephrology][52], [pain management][53], [internal
medicine][54], and [primary care][55] without the bureaucracy. From [Houston][56] to [Groesbeck][57]
and the rural Texas communities our doctors have always cared about, that’s the difference patients
keep telling us they were missing.

## Hospital affiliations

Our clinicians hold privileges at
[Houston Methodist][Memorial Hermann][HCA Houston Healthcare][Kindred Hospital][AMG Hospital]

What we treat

## Multispecialty medical care under one independent group.

Whether you're managing a chronic condition, working through new symptoms, or just want a doctor you
can actually reach — Remix clinicians cover the full arc of adult care, from kidney disease and
chronic pain to primary and internal medicine.

  Texas. We manage diabetes, high blood pressure, and heart disease. We also give checkups, yearly
  physicals, and same-day sick care. As your medical home, we team up with specialists and keep your
  full history on one record. The people who plan your care are the ones in the exam room.
  
  Learn more][59]
* [Primary Care
  
  Primary care is the base of good health for adults in Houston and Texas. We give checkups, yearly
  physicals, screenings, and shots. We also manage high blood pressure, diabetes, high cholesterol,
  and men's and women's health. You build a lasting bond with a practice you can reach. We offer
  same-day and video visits, and we refer you to specialists when you need them.
  
  Learn more][60]

Most healthcare runs on a corporate clock. The pieces — your primary doctor, your specialists, your
pharmacy, your hospital — all exist, but they don’t talk to each other, and the people making
decisions about your care aren’t the ones sitting across from you.

> Eight-minute visits, rotating providers, corporate referral loops — Remix Medical threw them out,

We’re a **physician-owned, independent multispecialty practice based in [Houston, Texas][51]** —
meaning your doctor decides your treatment, you see the same clinician every visit, and complex
cases get coordinated across specialists in [nephrology][52], [pain management][53], [internal
medicine][54], and [primary care][55] without the bureaucracy. From [Houston][56] to [Groesbeck][57]
and the rural Texas communities our doctors have always cared about, that’s the difference patients
keep telling us they were missing.

## Multispecialty medical care under one independent group.

Whether you're managing a chronic condition, working through new symptoms, or just want a doctor you
can actually reach — Remix clinicians cover the full arc of adult care, from kidney disease and
chronic pain to primary and internal medicine.

[View all services][58]
* [Internal Medicine
  
  Our board-certified doctors care for adults with complex, long-term illness across Houston and
  Texas. We manage diabetes, high blood pressure, and heart disease. We also give checkups, yearly
  physicals, and same-day sick care. As your medical home, we team up with specialists and keep your
  full history on one record. The people who plan your care are the ones in the exam room.
  
  Learn more][59]
* [Primary Care
  
  Primary care is the base of good health for adults in Houston and Texas. We give checkups, yearly
  physicals, screenings, and shots. We also manage high blood pressure, diabetes, high cholesterol,
  and men's and women's health. You build a lasting bond with a practice you can reach. We offer
  same-day and video visits, and we refer you to specialists when you need them.
  
  Learn more][60]
* [Nephrology & Hypertension
  
  Our board-certified team cares for your kidneys across the Houston area and Texas. We treat kidney
  disease, hard-to-control high blood pressure, kidney stones, and salt and mineral problems. We
  also give full dialysis care at nearby Houston units. As a physician-owned, independent practice,
  we share one record with your other doctors. You can see us in person or by video visit.
  
  Learn more][61]

  We treat long-term pain that has not eased with standard care, across Houston and Texas. Our
  board-certified doctors help with back and neck pain, sciatica, slipped discs, joint pain,
  headaches, and nerve pain. We use spine injections, nerve blocks, and nerve-burning (RFA). We also
  check if a spinal cord stimulator may help. We share one record with your other Remix doctors.
  
  Learn more][62]

  Our board-certified doctors care for the lungs and airways across the Houston area and Texas. We
  treat asthma, COPD, sleep-related breathing problems, and long-term cough. We offer in-office
  breathing tests, home sleep studies, and inhaler help. We arrange scans and lung rehab when they
  are needed. Your care stays connected on one record.
  
  Learn more][63]

  Our chiropractic team treats spine and muscle problems across Houston and Texas. We use spine
  adjustments, soft-tissue work, joint work, and healing exercise. We help with back pain, neck
  pain, headaches, sciatica, sports injuries, and pain after an injury. We work closely with our
  pain and primary care teams. Patients who need a team approach get it under one practice.
  
  Learn more][64]

kidney disease (CKD) patients experiencing iron deficiency anemia (IDA).

and older with CKD. The dosing for iron replacement treatment in pediatric patients with peritoneal
dialysis-dependent CKD, hemodialysis-dependent CKD, or non-dialysis-dependent CKD has not been

### Read the Important Safety Information

Known hypersensitivity to Venofer.

**Hypersensitivity Reactions:** Serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylactic-type
reactions, some of which have been life-threatening and fatal, have been reported in patients

iron sucrose; do not perform serum iron measurements for at least 48 hours after intravenous dosing.

#### ADVERSE REACTIONS

Adult Patients: The most common adverse reactions in clinical trials (≥2% and greater than
comparator) include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, hypotension, pruritus, pain in
extremity, arthralgia, back pain, muscle cramp, injection site reactions, chest pain, and peripheral
edema.

Pediatric Patients: The most common adverse reactions in clinical trials (≥2%) are headache,
respiratory tract viral infection, peritonitis, vomiting, pyrexia, dizziness, cough, nausea,
arteriovenous fistula thrombosis, hypotension, and hypertension.

#### Post-Marketing Experience

Because these reactions are reported voluntarily from a population of uncertain size, it is not
always possible to reliably estimate their frequency or establish a causal relationship to drug
exposure. In post-marketing safety studies of Venofer in 1,051 patients with hemodialysis-dependent
chronic kidney disease (HDD-CKD), adverse reactions reported by >1% were cardiac failure congestive,
sepsis, and dysgeusia.
* *Immune system disorders:* anaphylactic-type reactions, angioedema
* *Psychiatric disorders:* confusion
* *Nervous system disorders:* convulsions, collapse, light-headedness, loss of consciousness
* *Cardiovascular system:* bradycardia, shock, acute myocardial ischemia with or without myocardial
  infarction or with in-stent thrombosis in the context of a hypersensitivity reaction
* *Respiratory, thoracic, and mediastinal disorders:* bronchospasm, dyspnea
* *Musculoskeletal and connective tissue disorders:* back pain, swelling of the joints
* *Renal and urinary disorders:* chromaturia
* *General disorders and administration site conditions:* hyperhidrosis

Symptoms associated with Venofer total dosage or infusing too rapidly included hypotension, dyspnea,
headache, vomiting, nausea, dizziness, joint aches, paresthesia, abdominal and muscle pain, edema,
and cardiovascular collapse. These adverse reactions have occurred up to 30 minutes after the
administration of Venofer injection. Reactions have occurred following the first dose or subsequent
doses of Venofer. Slowing the infusion rate may alleviate symptoms.

Injection site discoloration has been reported following extravasation. Assure stable intravenous
access to avoid extravasation.

#### DRUG INTERACTIONS

Venofer may reduce the absorption of concomitantly administered oral iron preparations.

#### USE IN SPECIFIC POPULATIONS

Pregnancy

Untreated iron deficiency anemia (IDA) in pregnancy is associated with adverse maternal outcomes
such as post-partum anemia. Adverse pregnancy outcomes associated with IDA include increased risk
for preterm delivery and low birth weight.

Severe adverse reactions including circulatory failure (severe hypotension, shock including in the
context of anaphylactic reaction) may occur in pregnant women with parenteral iron products (such as
Venofer), which may cause fetal bradycardia, especially during the second and third trimester.

Pediatric Use

Safety and effectiveness of Venofer for iron replacement treatment in pediatric patients with
dialysis-dependent or non-dialysis-dependent chronic kidney disease (CKD) have not been established.

Geriatric Use

Dose administration to an elderly patient should be cautious, reflecting the greater frequency of
decreased hepatic, renal, or cardiac function, and of concomitant disease or other drug therapy.

#### INDICATION AND USAGE

Venofer^{®} (iron sucrose) injection, USP is indicated for the treatment of iron deficiency anemia
(IDA) in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD).

For additional Safety Information, please see [Full Prescribing Information][21].

You are encouraged to report adverse drug events to American Regent, Inc. at [1-800-734-9236][22] or
to the FDA by visiting [www.fda.gov/medwatch][23] or calling [1-800-FDA-1088][24].

  infarction or with in-stent thrombosis in the context of a hypersensitivity reaction
* *Respiratory, thoracic, and mediastinal disorders:* bronchospasm, dyspnea
* *Musculoskeletal and connective tissue disorders:* back pain, swelling of the joints
* *Renal and urinary disorders:* chromaturia
* *General disorders and administration site conditions:* hyperhidrosis

Symptoms associated with Venofer total dosage or infusing too rapidly included hypotension, dyspnea,
headache, vomiting, nausea, dizziness, joint aches, paresthesia, abdominal and muscle pain, edema,
and cardiovascular collapse. These adverse reactions have occurred up to 30 minutes after the
administration of Venofer injection. Reactions have occurred following the first dose or subsequent
doses of Venofer. Slowing the infusion rate may alleviate symptoms.

Injection site discoloration has been reported following extravasation. Assure stable intravenous
access to avoid extravasation.

#### DRUG INTERACTIONS

Venofer may reduce the absorption of concomitantly administered oral iron preparations.

#### USE IN SPECIFIC POPULATIONS

Pregnancy

Untreated iron deficiency anemia (IDA) in pregnancy is associated with adverse maternal outcomes
such as post-partum anemia. Adverse pregnancy outcomes associated with IDA include increased risk
for preterm delivery and low birth weight.

Severe adverse reactions including circulatory failure (severe hypotension, shock including in the
context of anaphylactic reaction) may occur in pregnant women with parenteral iron products (such as
Venofer), which may cause fetal bradycardia, especially during the second and third trimester.

Pediatric Use

Safety and effectiveness of Venofer for iron replacement treatment in pediatric patients with
dialysis-dependent or non-dialysis-dependent chronic kidney disease (CKD) have not been established.

Geriatric Use

Dose administration to an elderly patient should be cautious, reflecting the greater frequency of
decreased hepatic, renal, or cardiac function, and of concomitant disease or other drug therapy.

#### INDICATION AND USAGE

Venofer^{®} (iron sucrose) injection, USP is indicated for the treatment of iron deficiency anemia
(IDA) in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD).

Why bother

## You have the labs. You don't have *clarity*.

You drew blood. You got back twelve numbers, three red flags, and the feeling that everything is
fine and everything is wrong at the same time. That's the part we rewrite.

01 · Anxiety with no anchor

### The "normal range" isn't *your* range.

Lab reference intervals are built for an averaged population. Your age, sex, lifestyle, history —
none of that fits inside the bracket.

**Before:** "FERRITIN: 28 ng/mL · LOW"
**After:** "second drop in a quarter for you — recheck in 8 weeks"
02 · Charts with no meaning

### Is the line going up *good* or bad?

Most services hand you a stock-ticker chart. But health isn't a portfolio, and "trending up" isn't
always a win.

**Before:** 12-point chart, "↑ +34%"
**After:** "B12 has risen four months running — supplements are working, you can step down the dose"
03 · Advice with no owner

### Recommendations from *nowhere*.

An AI can fire off 14 tips in two seconds. But who decided they fit you? Who's going to do them? Who
checks they worked?

**Before:** "drink 2L of water and move more"
**After:** an 8-week plan with one task per week, and the owner is you
How it works

## Four steps from *PDF* to clarity.

Upload to understanding takes about fifteen minutes. You don't need to read the panel — that's our
job.

01 · INTAKE

#### Five minutes about *you*

Age, sex, goals, lifestyle. Enough for the report to talk to you, not to a "typical patient."

02 · UPLOAD

#### Drop the *PDF*

Any lab, any format. We pick out up to 340 markers. Nothing to type by hand.

03 · READ

#### A report in *sentences*

Not a table — a calm read. What matters, what waits, what to bring up with your doctor.

04 · PLAN

#### One thing *this week*

One task at a time. A vitamin, a recheck in 8 weeks, a consult. No checklist burnout.

Your report

## One report. One *link* for your doctor.

Every lab you've uploaded, in one place: the read, the prioritised plan, an overview of five body
systems, and the markers that need attention. Share a link with your doctor or download the PDF —
one click.

"I have three years of labs across three different labs. Used to live in a folder on my disk, things
would slip out of it. Now it's all in one place: I upload, and I stop tracking where the original
lives."

### [Coating And Paint Chemicals][68]

#### Coating And Paint Chemicals

YIGYOOLY is a professional China Coating and Paint Chemicals supplier. We provide Coating and Paint
Chemicals raw materials included titanium dioxde, acrylic acid, benzyl alcohol, barium carbonate,
butyl acrylate, chlorinated paraffin,dimethylol porpionic acid, fumed silica, glycidyl methacrylate,
hydroxyethyl cellulose, hydroxyethyl methyl cellulose, hypophosphorous acid, methy methacrylate, and
so on. YIGYOOLY insists on providing customers with high-quality products, competitive prices and
solutions.

Coating and Paint Chemicals mainly includes four major parts: resin, pigment fillers, solvents, and
additives. Resin is the foundation of coatings and plays a decisive role in the properties of
coatings. There are various types of resins, including rosin resin, alkyd resin, phenolic resin,
amino resin, polyester resin, acrylic resin, epoxy resin, polyurethane resin, organosilicon resin,
fluorocarbon resin, nitrocellulose, rubber resin, and so on.  Coating and Paint Chemicals pigments
and fillers mainly include coloring pigments, anti rust pigments, and extender pigments. Coloring
pigments mainly include titanium dioxide, lithopone, zinc white, lead chromium yellow, iron oxide
yellow, cadmium yellow, chromium oxide green, etc. Metal pigments include aluminum powder, copper
powder, etc. Extender pigments include calcium carbonate, barium sulfate, silica, etc., which can
reduce costs and increase the volume ratio of pigments and fillers.Coating and Paint Chemicals
solvents are volatile liquids that can dissolve and dilute resin or oils, change viscosity, and
facilitate construction. They account for a large proportion in coatings and paints. After the
coating forms a film, it evaporates completely into the air. Coating and Paint Chemicals

Additives play different roles in the production, storage, construction, and film formation stages
of coating, and have a great impact on the quality and film performance of coatings. According to
the uses, they can be cataloged into enhancer, anti adhesion agent, anti shrinkage agent, anti
flower agent, anti floating agent, defoamer, foam inhibitor, film-forming agent, anti gelling agent,
antioxidant, and so on. YIGYOOLY Coating and Paint Chemicals could help customer rise the coatings
and paints quality and performance.

YIGYOOLY Coating and Paint Chemicals have been exported to Korea, Morocco, Sri Lanka, Colombia, etc.
We established a professional team to serve customer of coating and paint industry, built a long
term business relationship with global coatings and paints customers. We have a great ability to
control coating & paint chemicals raw materials quality, lower down sourcing cost, provide high
efficient delivery, documents service and other service.

circulating water, cooling water, air conditioning water, etc. Water Treatment Chemicals

Scavenging, Scale inhibition, Corrosion inhibition, Antifoaming, Alkalinity Control, Coagulants,
Corrosion Inhibitors, Disinfectant.

YIGYOOLY Water Treatment Chemicals, with a professional and high efficiency working team, serve the
customers worldwide from Korea, Vietnam
